meetings.headline: Commission voted by roll call to seek an RTP planning grant for engineering at three conservation sites and a picnic-area grant.

Minutes were not voted on because the draft was not circulated, and an email/OneDrive migration and enforcement matters were discussed.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted by roll call, all five aye, to apply for an RTP planning grant for engineering at Table Rock, the Cowdery platform road and the Reno property.
It voted unanimously to authorize a grant application for a picnic area at the Small Town Forest.
Two certificates of compliance, for 90 Hemlock Drive and 37 Spring Street, each passed on a five-member roll call.
A resident asked for controlled discharge of water pumped from a water district test well near Hickory Hills Lake; staff will contact the district and it goes on a future agenda.
The December 7 minutes were not voted because the draft was not circulated, and no decision was made on moving from Google Drive to OneDrive.

why_it_matters: The grant applications would put town conservation land money, matched by state funds, toward engineering and a picnic area on public land, and the engineering cost was not yet known when the vote was taken.
The Hickory Hills well discharge question touches a lake and wetlands near homes, and the commission has so far only set it for a later agenda.
watch_next: The chair said engineering quotes would come back for a vote in January if the numbers are available.
The 23 Cove Road owner is to be placed on the first January meeting agenda, and the Hickory Hills well discharge is to go on a future agenda.

meetings.headline: Commission ordered the Baloney greenhouse moved out of the wetland buffer; it approved retaining-wall and delineation filings.
meetings.summary: The Conservation Commission opened with a hearing on an enforcement matter at 23 Cope, where a 10x10 greenhouse sits within the wetland buffer, and voted to require its relocation. It then approved a retaining wall NOI at 42 Pearl Street, an ANRAD at 400 Leominster-Shirley Road, three Lake Shirley retaining wall NOIs on Round Road, and two certificates of compliance. The chair also discussed possible grant projects for conservation land trails and parking.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted to require relocation of a greenhouse at 23 Cope that sits within the wetland buffer; the roll call was 4 to 1 as heard.
The applicants will work with the administrator on a schedule to relocate or remove the greenhouse, and she will update the commission.
The commission approved a retaining-wall filing at 42 Pearl Street and a wetland boundary determination at 400 Leominster Shirley Road.
It approved three Lake Shirley retaining-wall filings on Round Road, each with pre-construction meeting and construction schedule conditions.
The commission approved two certificates of compliance on Cross Road, and the chair and one member will pursue conservation grants due at the end of January.

why_it_matters: Owners with structures inside a wetland buffer can be ordered to move them, and neighbors citing past exceptions did not change the outcome here.
Lakefront owners planning retaining walls on Lake Shirley face approval conditions, and the commission's conservation land trail and parking grants may bring cash matches from the Timber rights fund.
watch_next: The administrator's update on the greenhouse relocation schedule and her review of old enforcement orders before the next meeting.
The amount of the increase to the kiosk materials purchase order, deferred to the next meeting, and the grant applications due at the end of January.
